subject: Social Media
title: Herbert Simon's Warning
description: A micro-lesson that makes Herbert Simon's Warning usable.

hook.text: In 1971, economist Herbert Simon wrote that information consumes attention. More info means less focus.

buildup.text: Simon saw it decades early. A world rich in data would be poor in attention. Supply and demand applied.

discovery.text: He coined 'attention economy.' Attention is finite. Every app, ad, and ping competes for the same pool.

twist.text: Simon won the Nobel Prize for other work. His attention insight was ignored—until Silicon Valley proved it.

climax.text: Today the average person sees 10,000 ads daily. Simon's 1971 warning became everyone's 2020 reality.

punchline.text: The scarce resource isn't oil or gold. It's your focus.

quiz.question: What did Herbert Simon say information consumes?
